claim: Stem asks which Roma player Grobbelaar's 'spaghetti legs' unsettled 'into blazing his penalty over the bar' in the 1984 shootout. Two of the four options fit the description: Bruno Conti (2nd Roma kick) and Francesco Graziani (4th) BOTH ballooned their penalties over the bar in that shootout, and Grobbelaar's wobble routine is attributed to both kicks in different accounts. Graziani is the canonical answer, but Conti is defensible on the stem as written.
q: Roma's fourth penalty in the 1984 European Cup final shootout, taken right after Bruce Grobbelaar's 'spaghetti legs' routine, was blazed over the bar by which player?

claim: Stem asserts Ronaldo's 1996 PSV-to-Barcelona move was 'then a world-record transfer'. The keyed answer (Barcelona) is right, but the world record in the summer of 1996 was Alan Shearer's £15m Blackburn-to-Newcastle move (July 1996); Barcelona paid roughly £13.2m for Ronaldo. Ronaldo's genuine world-record transfer was the following year, Barcelona to Inter in 1997. Sources conflict on whether the Barcelona fee briefly counted as a record, so this needs verification, but as written the record claim is at best contested and at worst plainly false.
q: Ronaldo left PSV in 1996 for which club, in what was then a world-record transfer?
